researcher_notes: No verifiable source states a specific year the Cameron IMPORT/regas terminal was mothballed. Documented facts: the original Sempra import terminal (Hackberry, LA) began operations in 2009 (offshore-technology market-data page, verified via Wayback: 'started operations in 2009'); Sempra decided to repurpose it for export and DOE authorized LNG export on 17 Jan 2012, with Sempra+Mitsui JV formed May 2013; first LNG export cargo May 2019. But the import terminal quietly went idle amid the US shale glut without any dated 'mothballed in YYYY' statement in any independent source. Sources give only a 2011-2013 conversion window, none of which is the mothball milestone itself. Per the no-weak-year rule, left UNRESOLVED rather than forcing 2011/2012/2013.

No independent non-circular source documents a specific 4-digit operating-start year for this marine terminal or the Valero Corpus Christi East refinery's marine operations. Lineage is well established (CLUI, TSHA, company histories): the East Plant is a ~115,000 bpd refinery 'built in the 1960s' that Valero acquired in 2001; traces to the Sinclair Oil Corpus Christi refinery bought by Coastal (Oscar Wyatt) in the 'early 1960s', then Coastal -> El Paso -> Valero (2001). Every credible source gives only a DECADE ('1960s'/'early 1960s'), never a 4-digit year, and none ties a year to the marine-terminal/dock operations-start milestone; 2001 is only Valero's acquisition. Genuinely pre-documentation; UNRESOLVED per the no-weak-year rule.
